flashcards.q: How does Delta Lake get ACID transactions on an object store with no cross-file transaction API?
flashcards.a: It needs only one atomic primitive: create the next-numbered _delta_log/*.json file if it doesn't already exist (S3 conditional PUT, ADLS, GCS all support this). Readers replay add/remove actions in the log to reconstruct which Parquet files are live at any version.

flashcards.q: What isolation level does Delta's optimistic concurrency actually give you?
flashcards.a: Snapshot isolation, not full serializability. Two writers touching disjoint files both succeed; two writers touching the same file conflict and one must retry or fail.

flashcards.q: What is the VACUUM retention trap and why does it break time travel?
flashcards.a: delta.logRetentionDuration defaults to 30 days (log history) but delta.deletedFileRetentionDuration defaults to 7 days (data files). Default VACUUM deletes files older than 7 days, so a VERSION AS OF query past a week can fail with file-not-found even though the log entry still exists.

flashcards.q: Z-ORDER vs liquid clustering - what's the practical difference?
flashcards.a: Z-ORDER fully rewrites every touched file on each run, so re-clustering a growing table means reprocessing already-clustered data. Liquid clustering is incremental - OPTIMIZE only touches files that need it - handles skew better, and lets you change the clustering key without a full rewrite. It's the 2026 default recommendation for new tables.

flashcards.q: What is Unity Catalog's namespace model and what does it add over the legacy Hive Metastore?
flashcards.a: Three-level namespace: catalog.schema.table (vs legacy two-level database.table). The catalog level gives a real access-control boundary above schema, plus automatic column-level lineage and unified governance across tables, volumes, functions, and ML models.

flashcards.q: What does Photon accelerate, and what doesn't it help?
flashcards.a: A native vectorized C++ engine replacing JVM-based Spark SQL execution for scans/joins/aggregations/writes, up to 12x on TPC-DS-style workloads vs naive Spark. It does not help Python/Scala UDF-heavy workloads, which still cross the JVM/Python boundary Photon can't vectorize.

flashcards.q: What's the difference between expect, expect_or_drop, and expect_or_fail in Lakeflow/DLT?
flashcards.a: expect logs violations but keeps the row; expect_or_drop silently drops violating rows; expect_or_fail halts the pipeline. All are row-scoped and can't express cross-row invariants like referential integrity or volume anomalies.

flashcards.q: Why is Delta's file format being open not enough to eliminate Databricks lock-in?
flashcards.a: For years the real dependency lived in the catalog (Unity Catalog), not the file format - governance, access control, and lineage all lived there. Databricks has since open-sourced Unity Catalog's core and added Iceberg REST Catalog server support to address this.

flashcards.q: Databricks cluster types and their relative cost?
flashcards.a: All-Purpose (interactive notebooks, highest DBU rate ~$0.55/DBU Premium), Jobs Compute (scheduled pipelines, 40-60% cheaper per DBU), SQL Warehouses (serverless option up to ~$0.70/DBU but zero idle cost), Serverless (model serving ~$0.08/DBU). DBU cost is separate from the underlying cloud VM cost.

flashcards.q: What single cost lever cuts 40-60% of a pipeline's compute cost with zero code change?
flashcards.a: Moving it from an interactive All-Purpose cluster to a scheduled Jobs Compute cluster - Jobs Compute DBU rates run 40-60% lower than All-Purpose.

flashcards.q: What did Databricks retire in October 2025 and what's the pricing floor now?
flashcards.a: The Standard pricing tier on AWS and GCP was retired; all Standard workspaces were auto-upgraded to Premium. Premium (Unity Catalog, RBAC, serverless, full Mosaic AI suite) is now the floor for new deployments.

flashcards.q: What does a timeout on a timed-out write NOT protect against in a Delta pipeline retry storm?
flashcards.a: Small-file explosion is the analogous silent failure: predictable maintenance being skipped (OPTIMIZE/predictive optimization disabled) causes read latency to degrade gradually over weeks with no hard failure, since every micro-batch write adds small files that never get compacted.

flashcards.q: What does the medallion architecture (bronze/silver/gold) actually buy you?
flashcards.a: Each layer is an independently queryable, independently recoverable, real ACID Delta table with its own lineage - if silver has a bug you rebuild from durable bronze without re-ingesting from source, and schema conformance logic stays separate from business logic.

flashcards.q: When is Databricks usually the WRONG platform choice?
flashcards.a: A pure BI/SQL shop with no ML/streaming/Spark workload - you pay for and operationally own a Spark-and-ML-oriented platform's surface area (clusters, Photon, MLflow) for a workload Snowflake or BigQuery serve more cheaply with less tuning.
